title: The PPO-ptx objective
goal:
Equation 2 in Section 3.5 is the objective that RL training maximizes:

$$\text{objective}(\phi) = \mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim D_{\pi^{RL}_\phi}}\Big[r_\theta(x,y) - \beta\log\big(\pi^{RL}_\phi(y\mid x)/\pi^{SFT}(y\mid x)\big)\Big] + \gamma\,\mathbb{E}_{x\sim D_{\text{pretrain}}}\big[\log \pi^{RL}_\phi(x)\big]$$

Write `ppo_ptx_objective(rm_scores, logp_rl, logp_sft, pre_logp, beta, gamma)` and return a float that estimates it from samples.

- `rm_scores` has shape `(B,)`: $r_\theta(x, y)$ for each of `B` sampled responses.
- `logp_rl` and `logp_sft` have shape `(B, T)`: per-token log-probabilities of the sampled tokens under the RL policy and the SFT policy.
- `pre_logp` has shape `(P,)`: $\log\pi^{RL}_\phi(x)$ for each of `P` pretraining texts $x$.

The response log ratio $\log(\pi^{RL}(y\mid x)/\pi^{SFT}(y\mid x))$ is the sum over the $T$ tokens of the per-token log ratios. Average over the samples in each expectation. With `gamma = 0` you get the objective of the "PPO" models; the paper sets $\gamma = 27.8$ for its InstructGPT ("PPO-ptx") runs (Appendix C.4) and $\beta = 0.02$ (Appendix C.4).
hints: A sequence probability is a product of token probabilities, so its log ratio is a sum of per-token log ratios. Use `.sum(axis=1)` on the `(B, T)` difference.
Don't average the log ratio over tokens. That would shrink the penalty by a factor of $T$.
The pretraining term is added with a plus sign, because the objective is maximized and a higher log-likelihood is better. Take its mean over the `P` texts.
